entries.title: Duplicate JSON object keys: Rust byte path keeps the FIRST occurrence, JSON.parse keeps the LAST
entries.rootCause: sonic-rs's borrowed DOM resolves duplicate object keys first-wins, while JSON.parse (ECMA-262) resolves them last-wins. For an input like {"name":"A","name":"Ada","age":36} against { name: z.string().min(3) }, the TS reference succeeds with "Ada" while the Rust path validates "A" and fails too_small. Fix direction: sonic-rs's Value object access must prefer the last occurrence (or the plan must treat any input with duplicate keys as status-3 fallback, since last-wins is observable behavior).

repro.refOutcome: safeParse(JSON.parse(...)) -> { success: true, data: { name: "Ada", age: 36 } } (last key wins)
repro.nativeOutcome: safeParseJson(bytes) -> { success: false, issues: [too_small @ path ["name"]] } (first key wins)
